questions.question: Which Chapter of Part VI of the Indian Constitution is concerned with the State Legislatures?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chapter III**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chapter III** of Part VI of the **Indian Constitution** specifically deals with the **State Legislatures**.
 
• This chapter encompasses **Articles 168 to 212**, which outline the **structure, composition, and functioning** of the State Legislatures.
 
• It also includes provisions regarding the **Governor, Legislative Assembly, Legislative Council,** and their respective **powers and procedures**.
 
• Chapter III provides a framework for **law-making** at the state level, ensuring that the legislative process is systematic and consistent across different states.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Chapter II**__

 __
 
• **Chapter II** of Part VI deals with the **Executive** at the state level, focusing on the **Governor, his powers, and functions**.
 
• This chapter includes **Articles 153 to 167**.
 
 
 
• **Chapter V**__
 __
 
• **Chapter V** of Part VI pertains to the **Comptroller and Auditor-General of India**.
 
• This chapter includes **Articles 148 to 151** and outlines the **duties and powers** of the CAG.
 
 
 
• **Chapter VII**__
 
 
• **Chapter VII** of Part VI deals with the **States in Part B of the First Schedule**.
 
• This chapter includes **Articles 238**, which was repealed by the Constitution (Seventh Amendment) Act, 1956.

questions.question: Which of the following dance forms is inspired by the sculptures of the ancient temple of Chidambaram?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Bharatanatyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bharatanatyam** is one of the oldest classical dance forms of India.
 
• It is traditionally performed by **temple dancers** called **Devadasis**.
 
• Inspired by the sculptures of the ancient **Chidambaram temple** in Tamil Nadu, Bharatanatyam reflects the poses and postures seen in these sculptures.
 
• The dance form emphasizes **expressive hand gestures (Mudras), intricate footwork, and facial expressions**.
 
• **Nataraja**, the dancing pose of Lord Shiva, is a significant icon in Bharatanatyam.
 
• Bharatanatyam is known for its fixed upper torso, bent legs, and intricate rhythms.
 
• It is accompanied by classical Carnatic music, and performances often narrate stories from Hindu epics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kuchipudi**__

 __
 
• **Kuchipudi** originates from a village named **Kuchipudi** in Andhra Pradesh.
 
• It combines both **dancing and acting**, often performed as dance-dramas.
 
• Kuchipudi focuses on **graceful movements** and strong **narrative** elements.
 
 
 
• **Sattriya**__
 __
 
• **Sattriya** is a classical dance form from **Assam**.
 
• It was introduced by the Vaishnavite saint **Sankardev** in the 15th century.
 
• Traditionally performed in **Sattras** (monasteries), it has strong religious and cultural themes.
 
 
 
• **Manipuri**__
 
 
• **Manipuri** originates from the northeastern state of **Manipur**.
 
• It is known for its **graceful, fluid movements** and **expressive hand gestures**.
 
• Manipuri dance is deeply connected to the **Ras Leela** tradition associated with Lord Krishna.

questions.question: In Jain Basti temple of Karnataka, over the garbhagriha is raised a ________ storied nirandhara vimana with a square griva and sikhara.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**five**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Jain Basti temple in Karnataka is known for its **distinctive architecture**.
 
• It features a **five-storied** nirandhara vimana, a unique architectural element.
 
• The term **nirandhara** refers to a type of vimana without ambulatory passage.
 
• The **vimana** is topped with a **square griva** and **sikhara**, characteristic of Jain temple architecture.
 
• The temple is an important example of the **Hoysala architectural style**, which flourished in Karnataka.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Hoysala Architecture**__

 
 
• The **Hoysala dynasty** ruled over parts of present-day Karnataka from the 10th to the 14th centuries.
 
• Hoysala architecture is renowned for its **intricate carvings**, **star-shaped platforms**, and **elaborate sculptural decoration**.
 
• Some of the most famous Hoysala temples include the **Chennakesava Temple** at Belur and the **Hoysaleswara Temple** at Halebidu.

questions.question: With which of the following festivals does the five-day long festival of Diwali end?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Bhai Dooj**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The five-day long festival of **Diwali** ends with the celebration of **Bhai Dooj**.
 
• **Bhai Dooj** is a festival that celebrates the bond between brothers and sisters.
 
• It is also known as **Bhau Beej**, **Bhai Tika**, and **Bhai Phonta** in different parts of India.
 
• On this day, sisters pray for their brothers' long life and prosperity, and in return, brothers give gifts to their sisters as a token of love.
 
• The festival is celebrated with great enthusiasm and traditional rituals, where sisters apply a **tilak** (a ceremonial mark) on their brothers' foreheads and perform an **aarti** (a ritual of worship).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Narak Chaturdashi**__

 __
 
• **Narak Chaturdashi** is also known as **Choti Diwali**.
 
• It is celebrated a day before the main Diwali festival and marks the victory of Lord Krishna over the demon **Narakasura**.
 
• This day is also known as **Kali Chaudas** in some regions.
 
 
 
• **Govardhan Puja**__
 __
 
• **Govardhan Puja** is celebrated the day after Diwali.
 
• This festival commemorates the lifting of the **Govardhan Hill** by Lord Krishna to protect the villagers from heavy rain and floods.
 
• On this day, people prepare and offer a large variety of food to Lord Krishna.
 
 
 
• **Dhanteras**__
 
 
• **Dhanteras** marks the beginning of the five-day Diwali festival.
 
• It is dedicated to **Lord Dhanvantari**, the god of medicine, and is considered an auspicious day to buy gold, silver, and other valuables.
 
• People also light lamps and decorate their homes to welcome prosperity and good fortune.

questions.question: In 1974, MS Subbulakshmi became the first Indian musician to win __________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ramon Magsaysay Award**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **1974**, **MS Subbulakshmi**, a renowned Indian classical vocalist, became the first Indian musician to be honored with the **Ramon Magsaysay Award**.
 
• The **Ramon Magsaysay Award** is often regarded as Asia's Nobel Prize and is awarded annually to individuals or organizations in Asia who have achieved distinction in their respective fields.
 
• MS Subbulakshmi was recognized for her contributions to the field of **music**, particularly for her exceptional talent and dedication to preserving and promoting Indian classical music.
 
• Her contributions to music and culture have had a profound impact on both national and international levels, making her a celebrated figure in the world of music.
 
• The award highlighted her role in enhancing the global recognition of Indian classical music and her efforts in cultural diplomacy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Grammy Award**__

 __
 
• The **Grammy Awards** are accolades presented by the **Recording Academy** to recognize achievements in the music industry.
 
• It is one of the most prestigious awards in the music world, often considered the equivalent of the Oscars in the film industry.
 
 
 
• **Right Livelihood Award**__
 __
 
• The **Right Livelihood Award** is an international award that honors and supports those offering practical and exemplary solutions to the most urgent challenges facing the world today.
 
• It is also known as the "Alternative Nobel Prize."
 
 
 
• **Pulitzer Prize Award**__
 
 
• The **Pulitzer Prize** is an award for achievements in newspaper, magazine and online journalism, literature, and musical composition within the United States.
 
• It was established in 1917 by provisions in the will of **Joseph Pulitzer**, an American-Hungarian newspaper publisher.

questions.question: Seleucus Nicator was a contemporary of ____________.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Chanakya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Seleucus Nicator** was a **general of Alexander the Great** and later became a ruler, establishing the **Seleucid Empire**.
 
• He had **interactions with the Maurya Empire**, specifically during the reign of **Chandragupta Maurya**.
 
• **Chanakya** (also known as **Kautilya** or **Vishnugupta**) was the chief advisor to Chandragupta Maurya.
 
• Chanakya was instrumental in the formation of the **Maurya Empire** and played a key role in the defeat of the Nanda dynasty.
 
• He is also known for his work, the **Arthashastra**, which is an ancient Indian treatise on statecraft, economic policy, and military strategy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kanishka**__

 __
 
• **Kanishka** was a prominent ruler of the **Kushan Empire** in the 2nd century CE.
 
• He is known for his military, political, and spiritual achievements and for promoting the **Buddhist religion**.
 
 
 
• **Ashoka**__
 __
 
• **Ashoka** was a famous emperor of the **Maurya Dynasty** in India, ruling from 268 to 232 BCE.
 
• He is known for his conversion to **Buddhism** and his efforts to spread Buddhist principles across Asia.
 
 
 
• **Kalashoka**__
 
 
• **Kalashoka** was a ruler of the **Shishunaga dynasty** in ancient India.
 
• He is known for convening the **Second Buddhist Council** around 383 BCE.

questions.question: With which of the following Amendment Acts of the Indian Constitution was 11th Fundamental Duty added?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**86th Amendment Act**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **86th Amendment Act** of the Indian Constitution was enacted in **2002**.
 
• This amendment added the **11th Fundamental Duty** under **Article 51A** of the Constitution.
 
• The 11th Fundamental Duty states that it is the duty of every citizen of India who is a parent or guardian to provide **opportunities for education** to their child or ward between the ages of **six and fourteen years**.
 
• The same amendment also introduced **Article 21A**, which made the right to education a **fundamental right** for children in the age group of 6 to 14 years.
 
• The **86th Amendment** is a significant step towards ensuring that every child in India has access to education.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **42nd Amendment Act**__

 
 
• The **42nd Amendment Act**, also known as the **Mini-Constitution**, was enacted in **1976**.
 
• This amendment added the **Fundamental Duties** to the Constitution, introducing **ten Fundamental Duties** under **Article 51A**.
 
• It also made significant changes to the Constitution, including the **curtailing of judicial review** and the extension of the term of the Parliament from five to six years.

questions.question: In November 2023, who was re-appointed as the Chairman of the Armed Forces Tribunal?
questions.solution:

__
 
• **Justice Rajendra Menon** was re-appointed as the **Chairman of the Armed Forces Tribunal** in November 2023.
 
• The **Armed Forces Tribunal** is a military tribunal in India that adjudicates disputes and complaints regarding the commission, appointments, and conditions of service in respect of persons subject to the Army Act, 1950, the Navy Act, 1957, and the Air Force Act, 1950.
 
• **Justice Menon** has a distinguished career in law, having served as the Chief Justice of the Delhi High Court and the Patna High Court.
 
• His reappointment ensures continuity and the application of his extensive experience in dealing with legal matters pertaining to the armed forces.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Justice Sharad Arvind Bobde**__

 __
 
• **Justice Bobde** served as the **47th Chief Justice of India** from November 2019 to April 2021.
 
• He was involved in several key judgments including the Ayodhya land dispute case.
 
 
 
• **Justice RF Nariman**__
 __
 
• **Justice Nariman** is a former judge of the **Supreme Court of India**, known for his expertise in constitutional law and commercial law.
 
• He has delivered several landmark judgments during his tenure.
 
 
 
• **Justice NV Ramana**__
 
 
• **Justice Ramana** served as the **48th Chief Justice of India** from April 2021 to August 2022.
 
• He focused on judicial reforms and the use of technology in the judiciary.

questions.question: Neville Steven Joseph D'Souza is associated with which game?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Football**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Neville Steven Joseph D'Souza** was an Indian footballer.
 
• He is known for being the first Asian player to score a **hat-trick** in an Olympic Games football match.
 
• D'Souza achieved this feat during the **1956 Melbourne Olympics**, where he scored a hat-trick against Australia.
 
• He was part of the Indian team that reached the semi-finals in the 1956 Olympics, the highest achievement for Indian football in the Olympics.
 
• During his career, D'Souza played as a **striker** and was known for his quick reflexes and goal-scoring abilities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kabaddi**__

 __
 
• **Kabaddi** is a contact team sport that originated in India.
 
• The game is played between two teams of seven players each.
 
• It involves raiding the opponent's half and tagging as many defenders as possible without getting caught.
 
 
 
• **Wrestling**__
 __
 
• **Wrestling** is a combat sport involving grappling techniques.
 
• It includes styles such as Freestyle and Greco-Roman wrestling.
 
• Wrestling is a traditional sport in many cultures and has been part of the Olympics since ancient times.
 
 
 
• **Tennis**__
 
 
• **Tennis** is a racket sport that can be played individually against a single opponent or between two teams of two players each.
 
• It is an Olympic sport and is played at all levels of society and at all ages.
 
• Major tournaments include the Grand Slam tournaments: the Australian Open, French Open, Wimbledon, and the US Open.

questions.question: Which of the two following countries were formed as a result of the partition of India?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**India and Pakistan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **partition of India** took place in **1947**.
 
• It resulted in the creation of two independent dominions: **India** and **Pakistan**.
 
• The partition involved the division of two provinces, **Bengal** and **Punjab**, based on religious demographics.
 
• **India** became a secular state with a majority Hindu population.
 
• **Pakistan** was created as a state with a majority Muslim population.
 
• The partition led to one of the largest and most tragic mass migrations in history, with an estimated **10-15 million** people displaced.
 
• Massive **violence and communal riots** accompanied the partition, resulting in significant loss of life and property.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **India and Sri Lanka**__

 __
 
• **Sri Lanka** is an island nation located to the south of India.
 
• Sri Lanka gained independence from the British rule in **1948**, separate from the partition of India.
 
 
 
• **India and Bangladesh**__
 __
 
• **Bangladesh** was originally part of Pakistan and was known as **East Pakistan** until **1971**.
 
• It became an independent country after the **Bangladesh Liberation War** against Pakistan.
 
 
 
• **India and Nepal**__
 
 
• **Nepal** is a landlocked country located to the north of India.
 
• Nepal was never a part of British India and therefore was not involved in the partition of India.

questions.question: The Permanent Settlement introduced by Cornwallis was NOT prevalent in which of the following regions of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Punjab**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Permanent Settlement** was introduced by **Lord Cornwallis** in **1793**.
 
• It was also known as the **Zamindari System**.
 
• The system was implemented primarily in the regions of **Bengal**, **Bihar**, and **Odisha**.
 
• Under this system, the **zamindars** were recognized as the landowners and were responsible for collecting and paying land revenue to the British government.
 
• The system aimed to create a loyal class of landlords who would support British rule.
 
• The system was not implemented in the **Punjab** region, where different land revenue systems, like the **Mahalwari system**, were in place.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bengal**__

 __
 
• **Bengal** was one of the first regions where the Permanent Settlement was introduced.
 
• The region was a significant revenue source for the British East India Company.
 
 
 
• **Bihar**__
 __
 
• **Bihar** also saw the implementation of the Permanent Settlement.
 
• The system had lasting effects on the agrarian structure and rural society of the region.
 
 
 
• **Odisha**__
 
 
• The Permanent Settlement was extended to **Odisha** as well.
 
• It influenced the economic and social dynamics of the region.

questions.question: According to the advancing of monsoon in India, which of the following cities receives rainfall after 15 June every year?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Jaipur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jaipur** receives rainfall after 15 June every year due to the advancing **southwest monsoon.**
 
• The **southwest monsoon** generally reaches the **Rajasthan region** around the second half of June.
 
• Jaipur, being in the **northwestern part of India**, typically experiences a slight delay in the onset of monsoon rains compared to the coastal and southern regions.
 
• Other cities listed receive monsoon rains earlier than Jaipur due to their geographical locations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Imphal**__

 __
 
• **Imphal** is the capital city of the state of **Manipur** in northeastern India.
 
• It receives the **southwest monsoon** much earlier, typically around the beginning of June.
 
 
 
• **Bengaluru**__
 __
 
• **Bengaluru** is located in the southern part of India in the state of **Karnataka**.
 
• It experiences monsoon rains in early June due to its proximity to the **Western Ghats**.
 
 
 
• **Hyderabad**__
 
 
• **Hyderabad** is the capital city of the state of **Telangana** in southern India.
 
• It typically receives monsoon rains in the first half of June.

questions.question: Which of the following sultans of Delhi set up three different markets for different commodities in Delhi?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alauddin Khalji**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alauddin Khalji** was one of the most powerful and efficient rulers of the **Khalji dynasty**.
 
• He is known for implementing several economic reforms, including setting up three different markets in Delhi.
 
• The markets were:
 
 
• **Grain Market (Mandi)** - For selling food grains.
 
• **Cloth Market (Sara-i-Adl)** - For selling clothes and other fabrics.
 
• **Market for Horses, Slaves, and Cattle**.
 
 
 
• These markets were established to control prices and ensure the availability of essential goods at regulated rates.
 
• He also appointed special officers called **Shahna-i-Mandi** to oversee the functioning of these markets.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Ghiyasuddin Balban**__

 __
 
• **Ghiyasuddin Balban** was the ninth sultan of the **Mamluk dynasty** of Delhi.
 
• He is known for his strict administration and for strengthening the position of the sultanate against internal and external threats.
 
• He introduced the concept of **Divine Kingship** and maintained a well-disciplined army.
 
 
 
• **Sikandar Lodi**__
 __
 
• **Sikandar Lodi** was the ruler of the **Lodi dynasty** and the second son of Bahlul Lodi.
 
• He is known for his administrative efficiency and efforts to improve agriculture.
 
• He founded the city of **Agra** in 1504.
 
 
 
• **Muhammad Bin Tughlaq**__
 
 
• **Muhammad Bin Tughlaq** was a ruler of the **Tughlaq dynasty** known for his ambitious projects and erratic decisions.
 
• He is famous for his decision to move the capital from Delhi to **Daulatabad** and for the introduction of **token currency**.

questions.question: Who among the following dancers won the prestigious Padma Shree award in the year 2021, for her contribution to folk dance?

__

questions.question: Which Article of the Constitution of India governs the Population Census?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 246**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 246** of the **Constitution of India** deals with the distribution of legislative powers between the **Union and the States**.
 
• This article divides the subject matter of laws into three lists: the **Union List**, the **State List**, and the **Concurrent List**.
 
• The **Population Census** falls under the **Union List**, meaning only the Parliament has the authority to legislate on this subject.
 
• The census in India is conducted under the provisions of the **Census Act, 1948**, which is a central legislation.
 
• The Population Census is carried out every **ten years** by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, India, under the Ministry of Home Affairs.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Article 179**__

 __
 
• **Article 179** of the Constitution of India deals with the **vacation and resignation of, and removal from, the offices of Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Legislative Assembly**.
 
• This article specifies the procedure for the removal of the Speaker and Deputy Speaker from their positions.
 
 
 
• **Article 233**__
 __
 
• **Article 233** of the Constitution pertains to the **appointment of district judges**.
 
• The article specifies that appointments, postings, and promotions of district judges in any state shall be made by the Governor of the state in consultation with the High Court.
 
 
 
• **Article 128**__
 
 
• **Article 128** deals with the **attendance of retired Judges at sittings of the Supreme Court**.
 
• This article allows the Chief Justice of India to request a retired judge of the Supreme Court or a High Court to sit and act as a judge of the Supreme Court.

• It is located in the **state of Himachal Pradesh**, India.

• The primary purpose of the dam is for **irrigation, hydroelectric power generation, and flood control**.
 
• The dam is a part of the **Bhakra-Nangal Project**, which also includes the **Nangal Dam** located downstream.
 
• The reservoir created by the Bhakra Dam is known as **Gobind Sagar Lake**.

questions.question: The zone where the earthquake waves are not observed is called:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Shadow Zone**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Shadow Zone** is a region on the Earth's surface where **seismic waves** from an earthquake are not detected.
 
• This phenomenon occurs due to the **refraction and reflection** of seismic waves as they pass through different layers of the Earth's interior.
 
• The **P-waves** (primary waves) are refracted by the liquid outer core and create a shadow zone between **104° and 140°** from the earthquake's focus.
 
• **S-waves** (secondary waves) cannot travel through the liquid outer core, creating a larger shadow zone that extends beyond **104°** from the earthquake's focus.
 
• The study of the shadow zone helps scientists understand the **internal structure** of the Earth, including the properties of the core.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Benthic Zone**__

 __
 
• The **Benthic Zone** refers to the ecological region at the lowest level of a body of water, such as an ocean or lake, including the sediment surface and some sub-surface layers.
 
• Organisms living in this zone are called **benthos**, and they include various species of invertebrates, fish, and microorganisms.
 
 
 
• **Hypocentre**__
 __
 
• The **Hypocentre** is the point within the Earth where an earthquake rupture starts.
 
• It is the location beneath the Earth's surface where the strain energy stored in the rock is first released.
 
 
 
• **Epicentre**__
 
 
• The **Epicentre** is the point on the Earth's surface directly above the hypocentre of an earthquake.
 
• This is the location where the earthquake's effects are usually felt most strongly.

questions.question: The number of organisms in the population divided by a regular unit of area or volume is called ______.
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**population density**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Population density** refers to the number of organisms in a population divided by a regular unit of area or volume.
 
• It is a significant metric in **ecology** and **population biology** as it helps in understanding the distribution and abundance of species in an area.
 
• This metric is crucial for **resource management** as it indicates how crowded an area is and can influence the availability of resources like food, water, and shelter.
 
• High population density can lead to increased competition among organisms, while low population density might indicate ample resources but also potential challenges in finding mates.
 
• Population density is often used in **urban planning** to design sustainable cities by assessing the human population in various regions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Death rate**__

 __
 
• The **death rate**, also known as **mortality rate**, is the number of deaths in a particular population during a specific time period.
 
• This rate is usually expressed per 1,000 individuals per year.
 
• It is used to understand the health status of a population.
 
 
 
• **Population size**__
 __
 
• **Population size** refers to the total number of individuals in a population.
 
• This metric is important for conservation efforts, especially for endangered species.
 
 
 
• **Birth rate**__
 
 
• The **birth rate** is the number of live births per 1,000 individuals in a given year.
 
• This rate helps in assessing the growth potential of a population.

questions.question: Select the INCORRECT statement from the following.

options.text: Both boiling and evaporation are bulk phenomena.

questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Both boiling and evaporation are bulk phenomena.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Boiling** is a bulk phenomenon as it involves the entire liquid reaching the boiling point and turning into vapor.
 
• **Evaporation** is a surface phenomenon that occurs at the surface of the liquid, where molecules escape into the air at temperatures below the boiling point.
 
• Since **evaporation** only affects the surface and not the entire liquid, it is not considered a bulk phenomenon.
 
• **Evaporation** causes cooling because the molecules with higher energy escape, leaving the remaining molecules with lower average energy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Boiling**__

 __
 
• **Boiling** occurs when the liquid's temperature reaches its boiling point, causing vaporization throughout the liquid.
 
• This involves the formation of bubbles within the liquid that rise to the surface and burst.
 
• It is a rapid process compared to **evaporation**.
 
 
 
• **Evaporation**__
 
 
• **Evaporation** occurs at any temperature, as long as the liquid's molecules have enough energy to escape into the gas phase.
 
• This process is usually slower and happens over a larger period.
 
• Examples of **evaporation** include the drying of clothes and the cooling effect of sweat on the skin.

questions.question: The iodine value of oil and fat indicates:
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**degree of unsaturation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **iodine value** is a measure used to determine the **degree of unsaturation** in oils and fats.
 
• It indicates the amount of **iodine**, in grams, that can be absorbed by 100 grams of a fat or oil.
 
• Higher iodine values suggest a greater number of **double bonds** (unsaturation) present in the fatty acids of the oil or fat.
 
• This value is important for understanding the **chemical properties** and **stability** of the fat or oil.
 
• Unsaturated fats are generally more **prone to oxidation** and can turn rancid more quickly than saturated fats.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **degree of saturation**__

 __
 
• The **degree of saturation** refers to the number of **single bonds** in the fatty acids of fats and oils.
 
• Saturated fats have no double bonds, making them more **stable** and less prone to oxidation.
 
 
 
• **number of iodine atoms present**__
 __
 
• This is not a relevant measure for determining the characteristics of fats and oils.
 
 
 
• **number of C atoms present**__
 
 
• The number of **carbon atoms** present in a fat or oil molecule does not directly relate to its iodine value.
 
• Carbon atoms are part of the fatty acid chains but do not indicate the degree of unsaturation.
